blogs.title: When FOIA Meets Counter‑Terrorism: How the D.C. Circuit Is Sharpening Exemption 7(A) Deference
blogs.description: This post dissects the court’s treatment of deference to the FBI’s assessment of a national‑security investigation.  It examines the case’s use of prior precedent—particularly CREW, Juarez, and CNSS—and explains why the court upheld Exemption 7(A) even after a three‑year lapse.  Analysts will find a clear roadmap for counsel on how to mount a FOIA argument when a law‑enforcement agency cites ongoing counter‑terrorism activity.

blogs.title: Segregability at the Crosshairs: The Fine Line Between “Reasonably Segregable” and “Inextricable” under FOIA
blogs.description: Here we focus on the court’s segregability analysis, evaluating the FBI’s categorical withdrawals and the agency’s justification that “non‑exempt content is tangled in exempt material.”  The article will contrast Mead and Perioperative Standards, explore the court’s reliance on ex‑parte affidavits, and offer practical guidance for plaintiffs who suspect too‑broad categorization.

blogs.title: Time Is of the Essence? Assessing ‘Pending’ or ‘Reasonably Anticipated’ Enforcement Proceedings After Years of Delay
blogs.description: This piece tackles One of the most contentious angles: does a three‑year dormancy sever the “pending” status required for Exemption 7(A)?  We’ll unpack the court’s reasoning, weigh CREW’s cautionary statements, and chart how future cases might reinterpret the temporal threshold for law‑enforcement investigations.

blogs.title: FOIA and the International‑Terrorism Context: What This Ruling Means for Non‑U.S. Nationals Pursuing Their FBI Files
blogs.description: Drawing from Farahi’s background as an Iranian national, this post explores how international‑terrorism concerns influence FOIA deference.  It will consider foreign‑national plaintiffs’ challenges, the interplay between immigration and national‑security investigations, and implications for media and academic researchers seeking similar records.
